parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs, manual argv parsing, bencode encode/decode, Python bytes repr, BigInt integer semantics, no forbidden typed-array or Buffer names, and /output placement requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent performed reference probing and assigned the whole implementation to one coder child; the parent retained final verification and final response ownership.
parallel.implementation: The child produced five library modules plus test6.mjs using plain strings for byte data, BigInt parsing, custom argv handling, bencode encode/decode, Python-style bytes and nested-list repr, and local-only imports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote the final files directly in /output, returned a completed handoff, and the parent read the generated files before presenting the output tree and code summary.
parallel.verification: Child checked samples, errors, quote/backslash input, BigInt, equals-form flags, and selected diffs against the executable; parent independently spot-checked samples, quote/backslash BigInt, argument errors, non-ASCII stdout emptiness, and forbidden-token grep.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 11 of 172 cases. Visible evidence shows the parent and child accepted a reduced non-ASCII stderr contract and relied on sampled checks, but the child lifecycle itself completed and was consumed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same migration requirements, including ESM files, manual argparse-like CLI behavior, bencode encoding and decoding, Python repr formatting, BigInt support, and output under /output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main actor owned all stages: reference probing, implementation, verification, final packaging, and user-facing delivery, with no delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote pybytes, pyrepr, bencoder, argparse, and test6.mjs; it used a PyBytes wrapper, BigInt parsing, bencode encode/decode, manual argument parsing, and imported node:path for basename handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial main actor wrote all files into /output and then delivered the complete file tree and code in its final response.
serial.verification: It ran sample diffs, several argparse and integer edge cases, and a non-ASCII comparison, then interpreted program-name and PyInstaller-only stderr differences as acceptable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 11 of 172 cases. The raw trajectory shows visible diffs were accepted in verification, and the final bytes repr implementation differs from Python quote-choice behavior for some strings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and child worked from the prompt requirements and an expanded child brief covering ESM, .mjs, local imports, manual argv, bencode, bytes repr, BigInt, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and independently probed executable behavior, including samples, errors, option forms, integer parsing, repeated flags, help, and non-ASCII behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the parallel parent translated the requirements into a child brief, while serial kept them locally. Both missed the official evaluator's full acceptance surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split reference probing to the parent, implementation and child-level testing to one coder child, then final checks and response to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, testing, and delivery in the main actor with no subagents or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run used delegation but not a multi-owner implementation split; serial was single-owner throughout. There is no unowned task stage in either trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief contained the source sketch, hard constraints, observed executable behaviors, Python bytes repr rules, CLI semantics, suggested module boundaries, and required verification steps.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor kept its own observed context and wrote modules directly, without handoff boundaries or cross-agent interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a parent-to-child context boundary, but the handoff was detailed and the child returned a usable summary; no missing, stale, conflicting, or overloaded handoff is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child implemented local-only modules named pyint, pybytes, pyrepr, bencode, argparse, and test6.mjs, using plain strings plus BigInt and no node built-in import.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented pybytes, pyrepr, bencoder, argparse, and test6.mjs, using a PyBytes wrapper and a node:path basename import in the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The module structure and byte model differ, but both implement the main sample behavior and both still fail the same number of official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed normally, returned a detailed summary to the parent, and the parent continued with verification and file reads before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; the serial main actor wrote and checked its own outputs directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a delegation lifecycle but no trapped, ignored, late, or cancelled result; serial had no comparable boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the child wrote the final implementation files; the parent later listed, tested, grepped, and read those files rather than concurrently editing them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main actor wrote all implementation files itself and then tested the same workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared /output workspace, but there is no evidence of concurrent competing writes, overwrite, final-tree replacement, or artifact leakage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child tests covered samples, edge success cases, errors, selected executable diffs, and forbidden-token grep; parent independently spot-checked several paths and read files before claiming completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample diffs, edge/error diffs, and a non-ASCII comparison; it accepted program-name and PyInstaller-only output differences as benign before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on sampled executable comparisons and accepted some stderr/program-name differences. The official evaluator later found the same aggregate failure count for both.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel took about 1181 agent seconds and 1306 cell seconds, used one child, did not time out, and finished with parent finalization after child completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial took about 533 agent seconds and 644 cell seconds, used no subagents, did not time out, and finished after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and tokens due to delegation and rechecking, but there is no direct evidence that budget pressure displaced required work or caused the official failures.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is both_fail: parallel and serial each have solution_passed false and the same 161/172 testcase count. The task-solving difference is process shape, not outcome: parallel delegated the full implementation to one child and then checked the child output, while serial implemented everything locally. The visible failing surface is better explained by ordinary implementation and acceptance choices, including locally tolerated stderr/program-name differences and incomplete hidden-case coverage, rather than by a parallel coordination boundary.
parallel_contributors: Parent probed reference behavior, delegated one full implementation task, received a completed child result, spot-checked output, and read files before finalizing.
serial_contributors: Serial main actor performed the same phases locally, wrote all files itself, ran samples and edge checks, and finalized with no delegation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel child used local-only imports and quote-switching bytes repr; serial used node:path and a PyBytes wrapper with a different bytes repr implementation.
Both runs accepted verification differences such as executable basename and PyInstaller-only stderr handling, leaving hidden official cases uncovered.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official failure data is mounted, so the specific 11 failing cases cannot be attributed beyond the visible trajectory evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; shared ordinary implementation and acceptance gaps, not a retained parallel coordination pattern
